routine.title: How Eisberg fits into your daily routine

items.title: Everything in one place (only 2 minutes of preparation)
items.text: Open the app and instantly see the complete picture: your last conversation, observations you've recorded, and the student's current progress. In just two minutes, you're fully prepared. No more endless notes or paperwork—every conversation begins with clarity, confidence, and focus.

items.title: Stay fully present during the conversation
items.text: Eisberg guides you through every step of the conversation with carefully designed prompts—from the opening, through goals and aspirations, to challenges and next steps. Together with the student, you create a personal empowering statement and a meaningful visual image that help keep motivation alive long after the conversation ends. Meanwhile, the app quietly transcribes everything in the background, allowing you to give your full attention to the student.

items.title: Automatic documentation
items.text: Forget spending hours writing reports afterward. Eisberg automatically summarizes everything that matters: strengths, competencies, goals, and next steps. Within minutes, you receive a clear summary that's immediately ready to be shared with parents via email—in their own language.

items.title: Voice note observations
items.text: Between conversations, simply record your observations as voice messages. Eisberg automatically assigns them to the correct student, so they're waiting for you the next time you prepare. Instead of starting from scratch, every conversation builds naturally on your everyday classroom experience.

items.title: Knowledge Hub
items.text: With a single click, Eisberg provides trusted guidance on student behavior, classroom management, relationship building, learning strategies, and parent communication. It helps you better understand situations, discover new approaches, and confidently plan your next steps with professionalism.

questions.question: What is Iceberg?
questions.answer: Iceberg is a tool designed to help teachers lead structured, meaningful learning conversations. It supports every step of the process – from preparation, through the conversation itself, to follow-up and parent communication.

questions.question: Who is Iceberg for?
questions.answer: Iceberg is primarily built for teachers and tutors working with students of school age. It is also valuable for schools and educational organizations that want to improve the quality of learning conversations.

questions.question: How does Iceberg work?
questions.answer: Iceberg guides you through three phases: before, during, and after the conversation. It helps you prepare, supports you with prompts during the session, and automatically creates summaries and parent communication afterward.

questions.question: Do I need to prepare before each conversation?
questions.answer: Preparation is minimal. Before each session, you get a quick overview of previous conversations, notes, and progress – so you can walk in prepared in just a few minutes.

questions.question: Does Iceberg replace my way of teaching?
questions.answer: No. Iceberg enhances your existing approach by giving you structure and support. You stay in control of the conversation – the app simply helps you do it more effectively.

questions.question: Is the conversation recorded?
questions.answer: Yes, conversations are recorded and transcribed to support documentation. Audio data is processed securely and handled according to strict privacy standards.

questions.question: Is Iceberg GDPR compliant?
questions.answer: Yes. Iceberg is fully GDPR compliant. Audio is deleted immediately after transcription (Zero-Retention), and no student data is used for AI training. All data is stored on EU servers.

questions.question: Can parents access the app?
questions.answer: No, the app is designed for teachers. However, parents receive clear and structured summaries after each conversation, so they stay informed and involved.

questions.question: Can I use Iceberg in different languages?
questions.answer: Yes. Iceberg supports multilingual communication, especially when generating parent emails, making it easier to include families from different backgrounds.

questions.question: How does the free trial work?
questions.answer: You can start using Iceberg immediately without a credit card. The full feature set is available during the trial, so you can experience the complete workflow.

questions.question: What do I get with a licence?
questions.answer: A licence gives you access to unlimited conversations, student profiles, automatic summaries, parent communication, and additional educational content and support.

questions.question: Do I need school approval to use Iceberg?
questions.answer: Yes. Since the app processes sensitive data, a data processing agreement and parental consent are required before using it in a school environment.

questions.question: How long does it take to get started?
questions.answer: Getting started is quick. Once the setup and required approvals are complete, you can begin your first conversation immediately.

questions.question: Will this add more work to my day?
questions.answer: No – the goal is the opposite. Iceberg reduces administrative work and simplifies documentation, so you can focus more on the conversation itself.

questions.question: What makes Iceberg different from other tools?
questions.answer: Iceberg is not just a documentation tool. It combines structured guidance, real-time support, and automated follow-up to improve the quality of conversations – not just record them.

iceberg.title: Why is it called Eisberg?
iceberg.text: We believe in the potential of every student. We also know how demanding the teaching profession can be. That's why we created Eisberg—to bring meaningful educational impact back to the heart of teaching. To us, school is about much more than grades and correcting behavior. Those things are only the tip of the iceberg. Eisberg represents the courage to look beneath the surface—to discover each student's true strengths, concerns, and incredible potential, while also recognizing and supporting the potential within you as a teacher.

shift.title: From daily friction to a shared system
shift.description: As a school principal, you don’t just manage conversations – you manage the entire system behind them. What happens in learning conversations affects your team, your parents, and the overall culture of your school. When there is no shared structure, problems accumulate. When there is one, everything changes.

bad.title: No unified standard
bad.description: Every teacher conducts learning conversations differently. There is no shared structure, no shared understanding – and no comparability.

good.title: A unified standard
good.description: All teachers follow the same proven structure. Conversations become consistent, professional, and comparable across the entire school.

bad.title: An overwhelmed team
bad.description: Many teachers feel insecure in learning conversations. They struggle to handle difficult situations and often rely on improvisation.

good.title: A confident, competent team
good.description: Teachers enter conversations with clarity and confidence. They know how to guide discussions and handle complex situations effectively.

bad.title: Eroding parental trust
bad.description: Parents experience conversations as unclear or confrontational. Over time, trust in the school begins to weaken.

good.title: Parents as genuine partners
good.description: Parents feel informed, involved, and respected. Trust grows, and communication becomes constructive and collaborative.

bad.title: Training that doesn’t stick
bad.description: You invest in professional development, but little changes in daily practice. What is learned rarely translates into consistent behavior.

good.title: Sustainable implementation
good.description: What teachers learn becomes part of everyday practice. Conversations follow a shared structure that reinforces itself over time.

bad.title: Conflicts land on your desk
bad.description: Misunderstandings escalate into complaints. Teachers feel frustrated, parents are dissatisfied, and you are left to resolve the situation.

good.title: Fewer conflicts, less escalation
good.description: Clear structure and communication prevent misunderstandings early. Issues are resolved before they reach you.

bad.title: No shared picture of the child
bad.description: Teachers, parents, and students see different things. There is no alignment on strengths, goals, or next steps.

good.title: A shared understanding
good.description: Everyone speaks the same language. Strengths, goals, and progress are clear and aligned across teachers, parents, and students.
